title: Why Do Cats Sleep 16 Hours a Day? 😴
description:
Why do cats sleep so much? Cats are hunters built for short bursts of energy, so they nap 12 to 16 hours a day, mostly in light 15 to 30 minute dozes with their senses still on, and only about a quarter of it in deep sleep.

topic: Why do cats sleep up to 16 hours a day?
script: Your cat sleeps 16 hours a day, but it's almost never fully asleep. So why all the napping? Cats are hunters built for short explosive bursts. Stalking and pouncing burn a ton of energy in seconds, and plenty of pounces miss. So between hunts a cat powers down to save fuel for the next one. It's most awake at dawn and dusk, when mice are on the move. That's why yours goes wild at 5 a.m. Most of its sleep is light dozing, in naps of 15 to 30 minutes, senses still switched on. One tiny squeak, and it's awake. Only about a quarter is real deep sleep, in bursts of 5 to 7 minutes. So your cat isn't lazy. It's charging up for the next sprint. So is your cat asleep right now, or just waiting?
key_facts: Cats sleep about 12-16 hours a day (PetMD, Hill's); PDSA average 15
Hunters that conserve energy between bursts of activity
Crepuscular: most active at dawn and dusk
Light dozes typically last 15-30 minutes, senses still alert (PDSA, PetMD)
About 25% of sleep is deep sleep, in 5-7 minute stretches (PDSA)
